title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. $\hat\pi_{0,3}$ is the profinite free group on two generators $x,y$ (the profinite fundamental group of $\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$). $M^{!\sim}_{0,3}$ is a group of automorphisms of $\hat\pi_{0,3}$, and $S_0M^{!\sim}_{0,3}$ is a group of pairs $(u,f)$ with $u\in M^{!\sim}_{0,3}$ and $f\in\hat\pi_{0,3}$, written as the product $f^{-1}u$ inside the holomorph $\mathrm{Aut}(\hat\pi)\ltimes\hat\pi$. The automorphism $u=u_{\alpha,\beta}$ is coded by a pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ of conjugators: $x\mapsto \alpha x\alpha^{-1}$ and $y\mapsto \beta y\beta^{-1}$ (presumably, with suitable normalisation). An element is therefore a triple $(\alpha,\beta,f)$.

Composition law. In the holomorph,
$$(f'^{-1}u')(f^{-1}u)=f'^{-1}\,u'(f^{-1})\,(u'u).$$
The product is therefore $(u'',f'')$ with $u''=u'u$ and $f''^{-1}=f'^{-1}u'(f)^{-1}$, i.e. $f''=u'(f)f'$. Computing $u'u$ on $x$ gives $\alpha''=u'(\alpha)\alpha'$, and likewise $\beta''=u'(\beta)\beta'$. This is formula (34). It has the same cocycle shape as Drinfeld's later multiplication law in $\widehat{GT}$, namely $f''=f_1(\ldots)f_2$ with one factor transported by the other's action.

Purpose. The previous page established $S_0M^{!\sim}_{0,3}$ as a semidirect product $M^{!\sim}_{0,3}[0]\cdot\hat\pi_{0,3}$, with the canonical subgroup $\hat{\mathbb Z}$ given by $n\mapsto(l_0^n,l_0^n,l_0^n)$. This page then transports the same structure to a 'model' group scheme $S\mathcal M_{\rho,\sigma}$ over a base $S$ (later $S=\mathrm{Spec}\,\hat{\mathbb Z}$). That group was defined earlier, at '(1)', apparently only as a set or scheme. It is now given a group law by declaring it a semidirect product (35): $S\mathcal G^*_{\rho,\sigma}\ltimes G$. Here $S\mathcal G^*_{\rho,\sigma}$ acts on $G$ through a homomorphism $\Theta$ (p. 499'). Elements $\mathcal U=(\alpha,\beta,\mu,\varepsilon)$ of $\Gamma S\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}$ play the role of $u$, and $G$ (with $G(\hat{\mathbb Z})\supset GL(2,\mathbb Z)$ per the next page) plays the role of $\hat\pi$. The isomorphism (36) sends $\mathcal U\cdot f\mapsto(\mathcal U,f^{-1})$; Grothendieck remarks on the identification of $f_*$ with $f^{-1}$ that this involves.

Next page. This yields a homomorphism $S_0M^{!\sim}_{0,3}\to S\mathcal M_{\rho,\sigma}(\hat{\mathbb Z})/\tilde\Sigma$, where $\tilde\Sigma\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^3$ records the three sign ambiguities (on $\alpha$, $\beta$, $f$). It also exhibits a normal subgroup $\mathbb G_a$. In short, it is a linear / algebraic-group shadow of the profinite Teichmüller-type group acting on $\hat\pi_{0,3}$.
errors: No genuine error. The formulas (34) are consistent with the holomorph multiplication under the convention $u_{\alpha,\beta}(x)=\alpha x\alpha^{-1}$, $u_{\alpha,\beta}(y)=\beta y\beta^{-1}$.

The coding of $u$ by $(\alpha,\beta)$ is ambiguous up to the centralisers ($\alpha$ modulo $x^{\hat{\mathbb Z}}$, $\beta$ modulo $y^{\hat{\mathbb Z}}$). So (34) is a law on triples lifting the law on $u$, not a law on $u$ alone. Presumably this is handled by a normalisation elsewhere, but it is not stated on this page.

Convention mismatch, flagged by Grothendieck himself ('identification au passage de $f_*$ et $f^{-1}$!'). The element is written $f^{-1}u$ in $S_0M$, but $\mathcal U\cdot f\mapsto(\mathcal U,f^{-1})$ in (36). Signs and inverses must be tracked carefully when comparing with (37).

ideas.what: Group law on triples $(\alpha,\beta,f)$ coming from the holomorph of $\hat\pi_{0,3}$: $\alpha''=u'(\alpha)\alpha'$, $\beta''=u'(\beta)\beta'$, $f''=u'(f)f'$.
ideas.modern_name: Composition law of (pro)finite Grothendieck–Teichmüller type groups (crossed-homomorphism/cocycle form)
ideas.where_published: Analogous laws appear in Drinfeld 'On quasitriangular quasi-Hopf algebras and a group closely connected with Gal(Q̄/Q)' (1990); Grothendieck's Esquisse only sketches the Teichmüller tower idea.

ideas.what: Defining a model group scheme $S\mathcal M_{\rho,\sigma}$ as the semidirect product $S\mathcal G^*_{\rho,\sigma}\ltimes G$ via $\Theta$, as an algebraic/linear target for $S_0M^{!\sim}_{0,3}$.
ideas.modern_name: Linear (GL2-type / abelianised) representation of the GT-like group; algebraic envelope
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas: Ihara's metabelian/Heisenberg representations, Deligne's motivic fundamental group (1989)

missed.claim: Within the Montpellier notes, Grothendieck sets up an explicit homomorphism from his profinite group $S_0M^{!\sim}_{0,3}$ (pairs (automorphism of $\hat\pi_{0,3}$, element)) to the $\hat{\mathbb Z}$-points of a group scheme $S\mathcal M_{\rho,\sigma}$ modulo $(\mathbb Z/2)^3$. This is an algebraic shadow of what became $\widehat{GT}$, written with the cocycle law later standard in Drinfeld's work. The computation on this page itself is routine.
missed.quote: nous allons y introduire la multiplication correspondante, ce qui revient à définir $S\mathcal M_{\rho,\sigma}$ comme un produit 1/2 direct
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical documentation that Grothendieck worked with a holomorph-type composition law on $(\alpha,\beta,f)$ in the loop-equation context, apparently before Drinfeld's GT. The mathematics on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine computation of a semidirect-product multiplication law and the setup of a model group scheme. Its interest is mainly historical, as a GT-like cocycle law in unpublished notes, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'la multiplication de $f''^{-1}$ $S_0\mathcal M_{0,3}^{!\sim}$ se fait' should most likely read 'la multiplication dans $S_0M_{0,3}^{!\sim}$ se fait'; the scribble is a word, not $f''^{-1}$.
In (35) the second factor is best read as $G$ in a semidirect product over $S$ (compare (36), $\times_S G$), not as a group '$SG$'.

Line 1: the struck-out expression is an abandoned attempt; the retained right-hand side is $f'^{-1}\,u_{\alpha',\beta'}(f^{-1})\,(u_{\alpha',\beta'}u_{\alpha,\beta})$, with the underbrace grouping $f'^{-1}u_{\alpha',\beta'}(f^{-1})$ (which equals $f''^{-1}$).
